checklist.item: Memory over time. RSS after N minutes of steady load, against the RSS at the start. Name N and the load.
checklist.evidence: timeout 420 bun memrun.ts <kit B> 5 30, exit code 0: a harness made of kit helpers (startOpsServer with an api-shaped registry of 20 checks, a JSON server with readJsonBody/sendJson, a failure limiter with the api policy, a logger). N = 5 minutes; per second 30 POST /results, 10 GET /metrics, 10 GET /readyz or /healthz, 200 failing /admin requests from new addresses (fills maxKeys, then overflow), 10 unknown paths; 80,418 requests, no transport error, 61,860 distinct client keys. findings.title: After a backward clock step, every new key in createFailureLimiter copies and sorts the whole key table until the clock passes the newest window start: about 1.2 ms per new failing client at 9,800 live keys instead of about 1 us
findings.command: timeout 120 bun limiter2.ts <kit B copy> <live keys> <step ms> with limit 10, windowMs 60000, maxKeys 10000 (the pulse-api policy) and an injected clock: fill the table, time 100 new keys (check + recordFailure), step the clock back, time 100 new keys, move the clock past the newest start, time 100 new keys; live keys 100, 1000, 5000, 9800 (9800: 4 runs with a 1.1 s step, 1 run with a 1 h step); plus timeout 600 bun growth.ts <kit B copy> (5 reps x 200 new keys after a 1 s step)
findings.unit: ms per new failing key at 9,800 live keys while the clock is behind (medians 1173.93, 1214.2, 1204.09, 1339.67 us)
findings.repetitions: 100 new keys per phase (median); 4 runs at 9,800 keys, 1 run each at 100, 1,000 and 5,000 keys; growth.ts 5 reps x 200 keys (1,000 keys 174.38 us, 9,000 keys 936.75 us)
findings.baseline: the same new key with a forward clock 0.32-1.83 us, and 0.35-0.70 us after the clock passes the newest window start again; cost while behind grows with the live keys: 77, 192, 749, 1174 us at 100, 1,000, 5,000, 9,800 keys
findings.budget: none: kit has no limiter metric and pulse-api has no budget for its admin routes
findings.impact: pulse-api runs check and recordFailure synchronously for each failed admin authentication (src/admin-auth-throttle.ts:79-94); during a backward step of the wall clock a failing client that opens an own window at 9,800 live keys blocks the event loop for a measured median of about 1.2 ms, not an upper bound. The sort repeats while the clock is behind and an own window can be opened; at maxKeys, new keys use overflow without a sort. Needs a backward clock step plus many distinct failing clients.
findings.fixDirection: Keep the start order without a full sort per insert, for example insert the new window at its position or re-sort once per step instead of once per key.

notes: Intl.DurationFormat is built at import (src/format-duration.ts:14): about 2 ms CPU per process (8 ms against 6 ms for an empty script, 20 runs), paid by every service that imports the kit entry; only status and notify call formatDuration.

The kit entry import grew from 37 ms (A 6a06ec2) to 44 ms (B) of CPU; about 5 ms are the built-ins of the new helpers (node:dns/promises, node:crypto, node:fs). Services pin older kit commits (api c6d2cba, probe 739188a, notify and status 236df21, console 536133f).

/metrics render is linear in the series (0.317, 2.274, 28.218 ms for 20, 200, 2,000 checks in the api shape, about 1 KB per check); the api collector rebuilds all check-state and budget series per scrape and Histogram.observe allocates a bucket array per call (src/metrics.ts:140-142), 488-561 ns per recorded result.

Logger: 8.3 us per line with 10 fields against 0.93 us for plain JSON.stringify of the same line (one replacer-based stringify per field, src/logger.ts:39-56); the faster-than-linear growth with nesting depth is the runtime's replacer path.
bun test test/<name>.test.ts exits 1 for 10 of 18 files with 0 failing tests because of the 80 % line threshold of bunfig.toml.
build_cpu_s is ok: nightly B 0.52 s against 0.6 s (87 %); B medians 0.302-0.517 s across 7 runs; local B 0.465 s, A 0.390 s.

Bench calibration (pulse-api scope): the same kit commit gave test_cpu_s B medians 0.465-0.768 s across 7 hosted runs; the kit budget has no per-metric floor override, so the default regression floor is 0.2 s; that floor does not relax the absolute 0.7 s budget.

The Docker A/B (timeout 30m bun bench/run.ts --a 6a06ec2 --b 536133f --rounds 2) was not run: for kit it measures the same bun run test and bun run build that were measured locally on both sides, and the nightly side B is the examined commit.
